role: Settings > iCloud & Data > Trash screen: lists intentionally deleted sessions (from RRCollector.checkForDeletedSessions), lets the user restore one or permanently delete one/all, with confirmation dialogs and a transient status banner.
types: TrashView: struct — SwiftUI View for the trash bin
SingleDeleteConfirmation: struct (private ViewModifier) — confirmation dialog gating a single permanent delete
toplevel: #Preview (lines 264-269) renders TrashView in a NavigationStack with a fresh RRCollector() environment. SingleDeleteConfirmation stores @Binding pendingDeleteId and let onDelete closure.

flags.text: Footer says deleted sessions stay for 90 days, but the only expiry, Archive.expireTrash (run at launch), removes only the trashed file; it leaves deletedIds and the raw backup, and RawRRBackup.purgeOldBackups is never called. checkForDeletedSessions lists every raw backup whose id is in deletedIds, so a session that had a raw backup stays listed in Trash forever and can still be restored from that backup.

USERS_MANUAL and in-app Help also promise 90-day Trash retention; deletedIds and raw backups of deleted sessions are never expired (expireTrash removes only the Trash file; purgeOldBackups is called only from tests), so raw-backed entries stay in Trash forever.

units.does: Replaces deletedSessions with RRCollector.checkForDeletedSessions(): raw backups whose id is in the archive's deletedIds, plus trashed session files in deletedIds that have no raw backup. Runs synchronously on the main actor.
units.entry: Called from .onAppear and after restore/delete actions.
reads: file:raw RR backups (index + every backup decoded via RawRRBackup.allBackups)
file:Archive/Trash/<id>.session (directory listing + decode of each trashed file)

flags.text: checkForDeletedSessions decodes every raw RR backup (allBackups -> readableBackup per index entry) and every trashed session file synchronously on the main actor, on every appear/restore/delete; SettingsPages+Data runs the same call in Task.detached to avoid this, so TrashView can stall the UI with many/large backups.

units.does: Marks the row as restoring, then in a Task awaits RRCollector.restoreFromTrash(id) (unmark deleted, restore kept trash file or rebuild from raw backup) and hands success (non-nil session) to finishRestore on the main actor.

flags.text: restoreFromTrash unmarks the session as deleted (SessionRecoveryService.restoreFromTrash) before attempting the rebuild; if the rebuild returns nil the id is no longer deleted yet nothing was archived, and finishRestore does not reload, so the row stays in the list though the session has left the trash and is not in the archive (a later reload drops it from Trash).

A failed restore is not rolled back locally: the id stays removed from deletedIds (only the iCloud state is re-marked deleted by abandon). The session therefore leaves Trash on next load; with a raw backup it moves to Lost Sessions, and if that backup has <120 beats the next Lost Sessions scan permanently discards it and its iCloud copy; a trashed-file-only session (e.g. imported workout) becomes invisible in both lists until expireTrash deletes the file.
No test in EmuquTests/EmuquUITests calls restoreFromTrash, permanentlyDelete, checkForDeletedSessions or expireTrash (grep); PageSnapshotTests only renders the empty Trash.

units.does: Clears restoring state; on success shows 'Session restored successfully', reloads the list and schedules the banner to clear after 3s; on failure shows 'Failed to restore session' which persists.

units.does: Starts a Task that sleeps 3s (sleepQuietly) and then sets statusMessage = nil on the main actor.

flags.text: The delayed clear nils whatever statusMessage is current, so a failure message set within 3s of an earlier success is wiped although the comment says failures stay until the next action; also sleepQuietly swallows cancellation, so the clear still runs.
